findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a bowl submerged in a soy sauce container. CORRECTED- the bowl was removed. Ensure ready to eat foods are handled with scoops that have a clear differentiation between food contact and hand contact surfaces to prevent bare hand contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed uncovered crepe wraps in the top drawer of the counter unit (right of prep area). The drawers are soiled and there was one immobile roach present on the side of the unit. Discussed keeping foods covered when in these drawers due to past pest presence. The pest problem has been an ongoing problem that is being handled. Adams is visiting two times a month. See General Comments for additional pest notes. The crepes were wrapped during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation.  (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the chemical sanitizers (sanitizer bucket and triple sink) to be at a low concentration (10 ppm Chlorine). CORRECTED- the sanitizers were remade to 200 and 100 ppm Cl respectively. Ensure chemical sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are made and tested at a frequency to ensure they are at the concentration as recommended by the manufacturer’s label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed spicy mayo in the refrigerator dated 6/6. CORRECTED- the sauce was made on 6/26, and the correct date was placed. Ensure  all food contact surfaces undergo proper ware washing, and are date marked on the day of preparation to be used or discarded within 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).[P]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed eel thawing on the dry storage rack (observed at an acceptable temperature). CORRECTED- eel was moved into the two door cooler. Thawing at room temperature is not an approved practice. Approved practices include thawing in refrigeration, cooking, or placing under cold running water.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.12 Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Slacking. Frozen TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is slacked to moderate the temperature shall be held: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the FOOD temperature at 5°C (41°F) or less; or (B) At any temperature if the FOOD remains frozen. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: The freezer top of the mini-fridge beneath the display/service area was observed to be coated with frost. Defrost the freezer so surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed that the Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) at the facility has not completed the allergen awareness training. Ensure that the CFPM completes the allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The facility has a few test strips to verify Chlorine sanitizer concentration. Ensure the facility has a supply of test strips that correspond to the chemical used for sanitizing food contact surfaces. Facility still has the test strips provided from the inspector during the previous routine inspection. New strips have been ordered and will arrive with the thermometer. Operator stated they are using the test strips to monitor the sani-buckets.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment:
It was observed that the operator was unable to properly communicate basic food handling safety as related to the nature of the operations. The facility is acidifying rice, using time as control, and serving raw fish. These are incredibly high risk food handling behaviors that can quickly cause a food-borne illness outbreak if not properly controlled. Staff should be aware of cold and hot holding temperatures. Staff should be able to acknowledge that foods held at room temperature should be used or discarded within four hours. There should be documentation of the prior handling of sushi fish so that everyone is aware of parasite destruction prior to use. Operator should also be able to demonstrate basic hand washing and control how staff wash hands. 
Proper hand washing should be demonstrated by all staff at the follow-up inspection. 
Staff should be aware of safe food handling strategies such as time as control, parasite destruction, and proper cold/hot holding.
findings.citation_text: 2-101.11(C) Assignment. (C) This section does not apply to certain types of FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS deemed by the REGULATORY AUTHORITY to pose minimal risk of causing, or contributing to, foodborne illness based on the nature of the operation and extent of the FOOD preparation. [Pf]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: The person in charge (PIC) was unable to provide Employee Health Reporting Agreements during today’s inspection. Inspector provided blank employee health reporting agreements during today’s inspection. Ensure all employees read and sign employee health reporting agreements to be maintained on file (at the facility) for future inspections.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).[Pf]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no bodily fluid cleanup policy within the facility. CORRECTED- Norovirus paperwork was provided during today’s inspection, and bleach is available. Ensure this policy is maintained on file for future inspections. Each food establishment must have a written policy for the cleanup/ disinfection of vomit and diarrhea to prevent the spread of Norovirus.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: The operator was observed beginning to prepare customer foods without washing their hands. Operator was previously in the lobby eating their lunch and handling other facility equipment. CORRECTED- The operator was paused from donning gloves to have a hand washing opportunity.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.11 Clean Condition. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall keep their hands and exposed portions of their arms clean. [P]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: The operator was halted from donning gloves in-order to wash hands. The hand washing process was halted multiple times in-order to achieve proper procedure. Initially, the operator simply rinsed their fingers and turned off the faucet and called that a hand washing. The operator then used soap for a two second scrub before turning off the faucet and reaching for paper towel. Finally, inspector interfered to demonstrate proper hand washing using a scrubbing timeframe of 10-15 seconds, rinse, dry with a paper towel, and used the towel to turn-off the faucet. SCDPH will be performing spot checks and education throughout the year to ensure proper hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Upon entering the facility, inspector attempted to wash hands but the hand sink basin was filled with a large bulk of steel wool. CORRECTED- the steel wool was moved to an adjacent counter to allow for proper hand washing. Sinks designated for hand washing must always be made accessible for hand washing ONLY. The sushi is rolled with gloved hands and hands should be washed prior to donning gloves.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink.  (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Required records available: molluscan shellfish identification, and parasite destruction.
findings.comment: The facility purchases sushi fish from Martinez (Sacramento Dr., Chicago). The facility does not have letters of guarantee for the parasite destruction. Martinez was contacted during the inspection and was aware of what paperwork needed to be sent. CK e-mail was given for records to be e-mailed. During the inspection, no documents were provided. Facility will receive a copy as SCDPH is provided.
findings.citation_text: 3-402.11(A) Parasite Destruction. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before service or sale in READY TO-EAT form, raw, raw-marinated, partially cooked, or marinated-partially cooked FISH shall be: (1) Frozen and stored at a temperature of -20°C (-4°F) or below for a minimum of 168 hours (7 days) in a freezer; (2) Frozen at -35°C (-31°F) or below until solid and stored at -35°C (-31°F) or below for a minimum of 15 hours; or (3) Frozen at -35°C (-31°F) or below until solid and stored at -20°C (-4°F) or below for a minimum of 24 hours. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket at the wait station to display no measurable concentration of sanitizer. CORRECTED- the sanitizer bucket was remade and observed at a concentration of 200 ppm Cl. Chlorine evaporates quickly, so ensure buckets are made and tested at a frequency to ensure the sanitizing concentration as recommended by the manufacterer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The facility is using time as control for the sushi rice but had some product from 10am the previous day. CORRECTED- Some of the product was kept for personal use, the remainder was discarded. The sushi rice is not controlled using a pH meter and thus should be discarded or used within FOUR HOURS. Time As Control for food Safety (TAC) paperwork was completed during today’s inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspectors observed various in-house mayo-based sauces sitting on the counter at room temperature (Spicy Miso Mayo and Chili Spicy Mayo). Previously,  the operator mentioned keeping the sauces on the counter for lunch and then put the sauces back inside of the cooler after lunch. The inspector educated about the danger of leaving temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods at room temperature for long periods of time and then putting them back inside of the cooler for future use. Previously, the recommended solution of using a time-as-control system where only small amount of sauce are brought out of the cooler and any leftover sauce are discarded after four hours was discussed. 
Today, sauces were again left on the counter and initially no one was quite aware of how long sauces stayed on the counter. Ensure that staff (there are only three) are educated on the proper time-as-control policy for house made sauces, spoons in water, tempura batter, and dry cloth on preparation counter. 
The aforementioned items should be removed/discarded and fresh created every FOUR HOURS. A Time As Control policy was created during the inspection. Discussed the bulk storage of sauces in the back cooler and movement of bulk product over 7 days.
Store homemade sauces, tempura batter, water and spoons, and dry cloth at room temperature for only FOUR HOURS.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed salmon in the standing double door cooler to be lacking date marking. The PIC stated the salmon was thawing. Thawing under refrigeration is an approved practice, however items should be date marked when brought into thawing. CORRECTED- the PIC stated they will be placing dates on the salmon. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are marked with the date they are brought into thawing in the future.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. [P]

findings.title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food.
findings.comment: The facility does not have a consumer advisory posted on the facility wall or within the menu. CORRECTED- inspectors provided a consumer advisory sign during the inspection. Ensure a consumer advisory is included in future menu prints. Facilities serving raw or undercooked animal foods must disclose associated risks of food-borne illness to the public.
findings.citation_text: 3-603.11(C) Consumption of Animal Foods that are Raw, Undercooked, or Not Otherwise Processed to Eliminate Pathogens.  (C) REMINDER shall include asterisking the animal-derived FOODS requiring DISCLOSURE to a footnote that states: (1) Regarding the safety of these items, written information is available upon request; (2) Consuming raw or undercooked MEATS, POULTRY, seafood, shellfish, or EGGS may increase your RISK of foodborne illness; or (3) Consuming raw or undercooked MEATS, POULTRY, seafood, shellfish, or EGGS may increase your RISK of foodborne illness, especially if you have certain medical conditions.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple white powders with no label. CORRECTED- the containers were labeled as sugar and salt. Ensure foods that may be commonly mistaken for other foods are labeled with their common name once they are removed from their container.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a wet wiping cloth stored on the counter during today’s inspection. Cease this practice. Wet wiping cloths must be stored in a sanitizer solution in between uses to prevent the growth and harborage of pathogens.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

Ensure the physical facilities are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris which may attract and harbor pests.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Facility was unable to provide Food Handler certificates for employees during today’s inspection. All employee who handle are serve food are required to obtain a Food Handler’s certificate within 30 days of hire. Inspectors provided a list of ANSI-approved programs that offer Food Handlers courses. Ensure all employees obtain a Food Handler Certificate by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed several dead roaches underneath equipment throughout the entire facility. Prioritize pulling out equipment to clean underneath. The inspector will check on cleaning at the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed after properly washing hands the PIC turned off the faucet with their bare hands and dried their hands using a multi-use wiping cloth. The PIC was instructed to dry hands with single-use paper towels and use the paper towel as a barrier to turn off the faucet. Ensure that employees always wash hands according to the correct hand washing procedure.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

(A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed various in-house mayo-based sauces sitting on the counter at room temperature. The PIC said that they keep the sauces on the counter for lunch and then put the sauces back inside of the cooler after lunch. The inspector educated about the danger of leaving temperature control for safety (TCS) foods at room temperature for long periods of time and then putting them back inside of the cooler for future use. The inspectors and PIC discussed possible solutions. The recommended solution is using a time-as-control system where only small amount of sauce are brought out of the cooler and any leftover sauce are discarded after four hours. This system allows the sauces to be left on the counter for convenient use during preparation. The inspectors will return on 10/15/2025 to check that the TCS sauces are being stored correctly.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed several prepared foods (i.e, various seafood salads) were observed in the prep cooler bottom without proper date marking. The PIC stated that the foods had been prepared yesterday and they will be used for several days. During the inspection the salads were date marked. Ensure that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the 7 day maximum (the day the food was opened/prepared being day 1, food is discarded after 6 additional days).
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed several roaches alive (slow moving) and dead at the facility. The number of roaches has significantly decreased from the last routine inspection; however, the PIC must continue to prioritize cleaning, covering foods, eliminating pest entrance points, and other pest control methods. They should also continue with routine visits from their pest control provider. The inspector will spot check the facility before the next routine inspection to ensure that the facility is taking proper pest control methods.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed utensils at the wait station stored with the food contact surfaces facing outwards. The waitress was educated and the utensils were inverted so the handles faced outwards. Ensure that utensils are always stored to prevent the contamination of food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned: 

(1) The debris inside of the sushi prep cooler bottom (currently not-functioning). 

(2) The debris inside of the mini cooler below the sushi prep station. 

(3) The debris on the trays holding clean dishes by the triple sink. 

(4) The buildup of grease and other debris on the handle of the toaster oven. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, grease, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed that the Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) at the facility has not completed the allergen awareness training. Ensure that the CFPM completes the allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed the PIC did not use a barrier to turn off the facet after hand washing. The PIC was reminded that a barrier must always be used to avoid re-contaminating clean hands. Ensure that the proper hand washing procedure is always used.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: THIS IS A 1st REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed various fish thawing at room temperature. Some of the fish was still frozen (at 41F or under); however some of the fish was observed above 41F. The fish above 41F was discarded during the inspection (four pieces of fish with internal temperatures between 50F and 56F). The PIC was reminded to thaw fish according to an approved method: (1) In a cooler at 41F or lower; (2) Under continuous running water; (3) As part of the cooking process; and (4) In the microwave. Ensure that fish is always thawed according to an approved method.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.12 Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Slacking. Frozen TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is slacked to moderate the temperature shall be held: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the FOOD temperature at 5°C (41°F) or less; or (B) At any temperature if the FOOD remains frozen.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Observed roaches at the facility. Currently the pest control company (Adams) only services the facility twice a month. The PIC should contact Adams and schedule more frequent visits. They should prioritize cleaning, especially hards to reach areas. They should also make sure that foods are covered and at least 6-inches off the floor. The inspector will follow-up on 5/1/2025 to check that the facility is taking steps to eliminate the pests.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed there is soiled water in the mop bucket. When mopping is not actively occurring the soiled water must be discarded (especially considering the presence of pests at the establishment). Ensure that soiled mop water is always dumped.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Observed the PIC was slicing cucumbers for sushi without wearing gloves. The PIC was educated that gloves must be used to handle ready-to-eat foods. Ensure that a barrier is always used when handling ready-to-eat foods to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed the PIC was filling up a sanitizer bucket in the hand washing sink during the inspection. The PIC was reminded that hand sinks can only be used for hand washing. Ensure that hand washing sinks are not used for any other purpose other than hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed eggs stored over avocados in the back silver double cooler. The PIC moved the eggs to the bottom shelf during the inspection. Ensure that raw foods are always stored below ready-to-eat foods to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the employee cleaning dishes in the triple sink was not properly using the wash, rinse, and sanitize procedure. The employee had a bucket filled with soap which they were using to wash the dishes and then rising in clean water before air drying. The inspector educated the PIC and employee about the proper procedure. Dishes must be first washed in soap, then rinsed in clean water, and lastly sanitized in a combination of water and the chosen sanitizer at the correct concentration. After education, the employee had three buckets set up for washing, rinsing, and sanitizing and was utilizing the proper technique. Ensure that dishes always undergo the proper wash, rinse, and sanitize procedure to keep food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed butane fuel stored on a shelf above the sushi prep cooler. The PIC was educated and moved the butane fuel to a new location. Ensure that toxic materials are stored in a position where they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, or single-use articles.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Observed fish thawing at room temperature during the inspection. The PIC moved the fish into the cooler during the inspection. They were educated on the importance of thawing using an approved technique (i.e, under continuous running water, inside a cooler, as part of the cooking process, or in the microwave). Ensure that foods are always thawed properly.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(A) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the FOOD temperature at 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed a cell phone stored above the back prep cooler leaning against clean dishes and a personal drink stored on a wire shelf above an open container of food. The cell phone was removed from the location and the personal drink was discarded during the inspection. Ensure that personal items are always stored away from food and food prep areas.
findings.citation_text: 6-305.11 Designation. (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed the employee working does not have food handler training completed. The PIC was instructed that all employees hired over 30 days ago must receive training in food handling principles. Ensure that the employee completes the training by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION from inspections dated 06/06/2023, 11/01/2023, 03/06/2024, and 09/23/2024. Observed several wet wiping cloths stored on counters during the inspection. Wet wiping cloths MUST be stored in sanitizer solution between uses. Due to the amount of repeat violations the inspector will follow-up on 11/12/2024 to ensure that wet wiping cloths are stored properly. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed an employee wash dishes in the hand sink and then start to put on gloves to handle food without hand washing in between. The inspector immediately stepped in and instructed the employee to wash their hands before putting on gloves. The employee proceeded to start washing their hands in the triple sink. The inspector stepped in again and instructed the employee to wash hands in the designated hand sink. At the hand sink the employee only washed their hands for about 5 seconds and failed to use a barrier to turn off the faucet. Ensure that employees wash hands when switching tasks in the designated hand sink according to the proper hand washing procedure. The proper procedure includes washing hands for at least 20 seconds and using a barrier to turn off the faucet. The PIC was instructed to educate their staff about the proper hand washing procedure. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
